# WI-06d-a Implementation — Debug geometry replacement in all critical-path areas

**Implemented by:** item-implementer role
**Date:** 2026-09-14
**Status:** completed

## Changes Made

### Production Code

**`src/world/worldData.ts`** — Replaced greybox terrain polygons in the coast band (band 1) with organic slabs generated by `generateOrganicSlab`. The coast band previously used manual rectangle definitions (WI-02/03 greybox geometry) that looked like debug geometry. After this change, the coast band terrain uses the same organic generation approach as the deeper bands, producing band-consistent terrain with irregular, non-rectangular edges (request §14.3).

Replaced shapes:
- `west-wall-slab`: manual 4-point rectangle → `slab('west-wall-slab', -2560, -1282, 64, 382, 1)`
- `wall-slab`: manual 4-point rectangle → `slab('wall-slab', 2370, -1000, 64, 1000, 1)`
- `ridge-slab`: manual 4-point rectangle → `slab('ridge-slab', 4700, -1000, 64, 1000, 1)`
- `seal-slab`: manual 4-point rectangle → `slab('seal-slab', -1260, -1600, 120, 1600, 1)`

The `seabed-floor` shape was kept as-is because it has a special open-ended shape with a descent notch that cannot be represented as a simple slab.

### Tests

**`src/world/coastOrganicTerrain.test.ts`** — Added 3 new tests to verify the coast band terrain uses organic slabs:
- `coast band terrain shapes have organic visual outlines (>4 points)` — verifies organic visual outlines
- `coast band terrain shapes are closed organic slabs` — verifies all shapes are closed
- `all coast band chunks use organic terrain (no greybox polygons)` — verifies every terrain shape has an organic visual outline

All 3 tests pass. Full suite: 370 passed, 2 pre-existing failures in simulation/creature tier tests (unrelated to this work item).

## Notes for Reviewer

- The coast band is the only band that still used greybox geometry after WI-06a/b/c. This work item completes the geometry replacement for all critical-path areas.
- The `seabed-floor` shape has a special open-ended shape with a descent notch that cannot be represented as a simple slab, so it was kept as-is.
- The `slab()` helper generates a rectangular collision shape with an organic visual outline, which is exactly what's needed for the hanging pillars and walls.
- The 2 pre-existing test failures (`tier3Scenario.test.ts` and `rosterFinalProof.test.ts`) are about creature spawn placement (T-17 in chunk shelf band 2) and are unrelated to the terrain changes.
